---
title: "Homework"
---

Six notebooks, one per unit-pair, each built on the same **verify-then-apply**
arc that runs through the whole course: do the problem by hand, watch the
toolbox reproduce your number, then use the now-trusted tool to answer the
question that was too tedious for paper.

Open any notebook in Colab or Jupyter; the first cell installs the toolbox
(uncomment the `%pip` line on first run).

| # | Notebook | Units | Anchored on |
|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | `hw1-properties-dimensions` | 1–2 | a rheometer that hides its yield stress; the Buckingham bubble; a 1:25 Froude spillway |
| 2 | `hw2-hydrostatics` | 3 | gate + hinge reaction; a suction-tank manometer walk; barge stability with deck cargo |
| 3 | `hw3-bernoulli-cv` | 4–5 | two holes / equal range; venturi-vs-orifice five-year rent; firefighter recoil |
| 4 | `hw4-profiles-external` | 6–7 | Couette backflow onset; a towed plate's drag; the knuckleball Reynolds number and hail |
| 5 | `hw5-pipeflow-pumps` | 8 | the (legally dubious) fire hydrant; a shower loss-audit; **pick-a-pump A/B/C**; throttle vs. VFD |
| 6 | `hw6-channels-turbo` | 9–10 | a stilling-basin's megawatts; a canal that needs mowing; specific-speed machine safari; Pelton's ½ |

::: {.callout-note}
### For instructors
Worked solution notebooks live in `homework/solutions/` — every hand
calculation shown, every code cell executed, so the printed numbers are the
ones to expect. They are `.gitignore`d so a public push won't publish them; distribute
via your LMS.
:::

::: {.callout-tip}
### The pump problem is the capstone
Homework 5, Problem 3 is the course in miniature: three real pump curves, a
piping system students have been building since Unit 8, and a decision that
punishes both the cheapest sticker (B costs \$2,300 more to *own*) and the
biggest pump (A cavitates at −2.47 m and is disqualified on the spot). The
answer is C, and the memo they write to justify it is the assessment.
:::
